surprises.description: ARE recorded $638 million of real estate impairments, far above the preview’s downside scenario of another $150 million or more. The charge was concentrated, with the two largest impairments accounting for 75% of the total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recognized $638 million in real estate impairments during the quarter,” with “the two largest impairments” making up “75% of the total.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “another large charge” as a risk and set the bear case at “another $150M+ impairment.”

surprises.description: Leasing reached 1.24 million square feet, well above the roughly 950,000 square feet the preview said management had guided for, and included 451,000 square feet of previously vacant space. The total was the highest in seven quarters, with vacant-space leasing the second-largest quarterly amount in company history.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 leasing volume reached 1.24 million square feet (highest in 7 quarters)” and “Leasing of previously vacant space totaled 451,000 square feet, the second-largest quarterly amount in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management guided “~950k RSF for 3Q”; the preview’s base case expected “leasing ~900–950k RSF.”

surprises.description: Cash same-property NOI declined only 2.8%, substantially better than the preview’s consensus expectation of a 19.3% decline. Reported same-property NOI was still down 6.7%, but the cash result was much less weak than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same property NOI declined 6.7% (down 2.8% on a cash basis).”

surprises.description: Quarter-end occupancy was 87.1%, above the preview’s 85.9–86.1% expectation. That is a stronger reported occupancy level than anticipated, although the preview had also highlighted a signed-lease backlog that could lift occupancy later.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Occupancy ended Q3 at 87.1%, up 20 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Occupancy … 86.1% street / 85.9% Zacks model.”

surprises.description: Completed and pending dispositions totaled $2.6 billion, below the preview’s approximately $2.9 billion disposition target, and management said some proceeds may be deferred into 2027. The amount exceeded the $1.9 billion midpoint referenced on the call, but still fell short of the preview’s stated target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed and pending dispositions total $2.6 billion,” with “potential deferral of some proceeds into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “dispositions ~$2.9B” in standing FY2026 guidance and called $2.9 billion the target.

surprises.description: ARE disclosed an unusually large post-quarter capital raise and financing package: $1 billion of hybrid notes carrying a 7.25% rate and a $475 million Campus Point JV with a minimum 5.5% distribution and a put right after seven years. The preview had discussed deleveraging and no common equity issuance, but did not anticipate these specific financing terms or structures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed $1.7 billion of capital since June 30,” including “a $1 billion junior subordinated (hybrid) notes offering at 7.25% receiving 50% equity credit” and “a $475 million Campus Point JV with a minimum 5.5% distribution and a put right after 7 years.”

surprises.description: Management identified another $30–35 million of tenant wind-downs in 2027, similar to 2026, adding a specific continuing headwind to the already weak outlook. The preview anticipated 2027 pressure but did not identify this recurring wind-down amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged “continued tenant wind-downs estimated at $30-35 million similar to 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted BMO’s forecast of “2027 core FFO −26% YoY” but did not state an expectation for $30–35 million of tenant wind-downs.

surprises.description: The development and redevelopment pipeline had contracted by more than half since Q4 2025, while capitalized interest also fell. This points to a sharper reduction in development activity than the preview’s snapshot of 1.4 million square feet under construction suggested, though the smaller pipeline also reduces near-term capitalized interest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The development/redevelopment pipeline shrank over 50% (from 3.6 million to 1.6 million square feet) since Q4 2025,” and “capitalized interest fell $11 million to $62.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “1.4M RSF under construction, 71% leased,” but did not forecast a reduction in the broader pipeline.

surprises.description: Public biotech accounted for only 1.1% of leasing, below the 6% share cited for the prior quarter in the preview. The continued low share reinforces that leasing was being driven by tenants outside public biotech, rather than a clear return of that tenant group.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Public biotech represented only 1.1% of total leasing volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “public biotech was just 6% of 2Q leasing” and flagged tenant mix as something to watch.

surprises.description: ARE reaffirmed its $6.40 full-year FFO midpoint but tightened the full-year range to plus or minus $0.02. The unchanged midpoint was expected; the narrower range was a modestly firmer statement of confidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 FFO midpoint of $6.40 while tightening the range to plus or minus $0.02.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed standing FY2026 FFO guidance of “$6.35–$6.45 (midpoint $6.40).”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted FFO per share of $1.54 modestly exceeded the preview’s $1.52–$1.53 consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FFO per share diluted as adjusted was $1.54 for Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited consensus of “$1.52 (Zacks) / $1.53 (alt. compilers).”
